findings.resolution: Fixed by locally typed lifecycle failures and safe terminal wrapping at manager getPlaybackUrl boundary. Repeated actual manager+coordinator+public QQ resolver counterexample now returns provider.playbackUnavailable, sends one cancellation, suppresses the late utility result, and leaves zero pending calls.

boundaries: Provider alone owns QQ finite same-track fallback order and persisted preference; same exact TrackInfo/queue identity retained
Explicit missing flag skips; unknown may verify; each candidate at most once; no upgrade or cross-spatial fallback
Only per-run privately attributed missing/empty/observed22 errors continue; auth/network/unknown/key/header/container failures terminal
Full session, epoch and AbortSignal ownership checked before next candidate and publication; failed or late opened leases revoked
Successful lease remains on one resolver and actualQuality/bytes envelope; Range refresh cannot change format
Terminal code is checked before queue search, cross-source fallback, rematch or library replacement; stable flags settle
Local RPC active/queued timeout, cancellation, host stop/wake failure, overload/circuit and dispatch errors use a typed local boundary with fixed safe reason
Remote provider business errors cannot forge local lifecycle type; old unmarked remote failures and non-playback message behavior remain compatible
Latest progress/pause and cancellation/owner guards retained; unresolved quality leaves existing stream intact
retirement: Removed the host controller catalogue veto now superseded by provider same-track downgrade; original cross-source recovery remains only for unmarked business failures. No second preference or QQ-specific host fallback chain was added.
